title: Rethinking Visual Attribution for Chest X-ray Reasoning in Large Vision Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2605.20158v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) show promise in medical applications, but their inability to faithfully ground responses in visual evidence raises serious concerns about clinical trustworthiness. While visual attribution methods are widely used to explain LVLM predictions, whether these explanations actually reflect the visual evidence underlying the model's decision is largely unverified, since ground-truth annotations for internal model reasoning are typically unavailable. We address this question for chest X-ray (CXR) reasoning by developing a causal evaluation framework that retains only CXR-VQA samples for which the expert-annotated region is verified, via counterfactual editing, to be causally responsible for the model's prediction. translated_title: 重新思考大型视觉语言模型中胸部X光推理的视觉归因方法
translated_abstract: 大型视觉语言模型（LVLMs）在医疗应用中展现出巨大潜力，但其无法将回答忠实锚定于视觉证据，这引发了对临床可信度的严重担忧。虽然视觉归因方法被广泛用于解释LVLM的预测，但这些解释是否真正反映了模型决策背后的视觉证据在很大程度上尚未得到验证，因为模型内部推理的真值标注通常是不可获得的。我们通过开发一个因果评估框架来解决胸部X光（CXR）推理中的这一问题，该框架仅保留那些经反事实编辑验证其专家标注区域对模型预测具有因果责任的CXR-VQA样本。利用该框架，我们在11种归因方法、六个开源LVLM以及两种输出模式（直接回答和逐步推理）上进行评估，发现现有的归因方法往往……（原文摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了一个基于反事实编辑的因果评估框架，用于验证视觉归因方法是否真正反映了大型视觉语言模型在胸部X光推理中决策所依赖的视觉证据，并发现现有归因方法在该框架下并不可靠。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a causal evaluation framework based on counterfactual editing to verify whether visual attribution methods faithfully reflect the visual evidence underlying LVLMs' chest X-ray reasoning, revealing that existing attribution methods are often unreliable under this framework.
